title: MCP Ecosystem & Community
content:
## What Is MCP?

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard, published by Anthropic, that defines how AI models connect to external tools and data sources. It standardizes the interface between a model (client) and a capability provider (server) the same way USB-C standardizes physical connectors: any compliant server works with any compliant client, regardless of who built either side.

For a technical overview of MCP's function-calling mechanics and how to build servers, see [Tool Use & Agents](tool-use-and-agents).

This page covers the community ecosystem that has grown around the standard.

---

## Server Ecosystem Scale

As of early 2026, over **500 public MCP servers** are indexed in community registries. Major categories:

| Category | Example Servers |
|---|---|
| Databases | Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, Snowflake |
| File storage | Google Drive, Dropbox, Box, S3 |
| Developer tools | GitHub, GitLab, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform |
| Communication | Slack, email (Gmail/Outlook), Discord, Teams |
| Project mgmt | Jira, Asana, Linear, Notion |
| Payments & commerce | Stripe, Shopify |
| Design | Figma, Canva |
| Web | Browser automation, search, scraping |
| Legal | 20+ connectors for legal research, contracts, discovery |

The community adds new servers weekly; the pace has accelerated as more LLM providers adopted MCP as their native tool interface.

---

## Official Registries and Discovery Tools

**Anthropic's official servers** are maintained in the [`modelcontextprotocol/servers`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers) GitHub repository. This includes reference implementations for filesystem access, web fetch, memory, and several first-party integrations.

**Community registries:**
- **MCP Registry** (modelcontextprotocol.io/registry) — the canonical index, curated by the MCP governance team
- **MCPHub** — open-source desktop GUI for macOS and Windows; browse, install, and manage servers without editing JSON config files
- **MCPRepository.com** — community-maintained catalog with search, filtering by category, and install instructions

---

## Governance Model

MCP transitioned from Anthropic-internal spec to community governance in late 2025. The current model:

- **Spec Enhancement Proposals (SEPs):** Anyone can submit an SEP via GitHub. The MCP team reviews, labels, and schedules accepted proposals for implementation.
- **Working Groups:** Focused groups address specific concern areas — security, transport layers, multi-modal data, and server discovery. Working group outputs feed into SEPs.
- **Steering committee:** Representatives from Anthropic and major adopting companies (including several large cloud providers) hold monthly synchronous meetings; notes are published publicly.

This governance structure mirrors successful open standards like OpenAPI and JSON Schema — protocol stability is owned by the community, not a single vendor.

---

## 2026 Roadmap Highlights

The published MCP 2026 roadmap (blog.modelcontextprotocol.io) includes several significant items:

**Streaming responses from servers:** Currently, MCP servers return a single response to a tool call. Streaming support will let servers emit partial results as they arrive — useful for long-running database queries or web scrapes.

**Server-initiated messages:** Allows a server to push notifications to the client (e.g., a Slack MCP server notifying the agent when a relevant message appears), enabling reactive rather than purely request-driven agents.

**Multi-modal tool results:** Standardized handling for tool results that return images, audio, or structured documents, not just text/JSON.

**Authorization delegation:** An OAuth-based pattern allowing a server to request scoped credentials on behalf of the user, rather than requiring static API keys in configuration.

---

## Adoption Beyond Claude

MCP has been adopted as the tool interface by multiple LLM providers and frameworks beyond Anthropic. As of mid-2026, client support is present in OpenAI's API, Google's Gemini, and all major open-source orchestration frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, AutoGen). This means community-built MCP servers are reusable across different AI stacks — a server written for Claude works equally well with a competing model.
